title: Then go out and seek
hook: when the prayer is done, disperse and seek Allah's bounty (62:10)

segments.voice: Yesterday, khutbah, the Friday sermon, and your line was leave trade for a while. What did you arrive early to, and what did the waiting feel like? Day six hundred twenty-seven.

The Friday prayer ends. People stand, shake hands, find their shoes in the pile by the door. Within ten minutes, the shutters are back up, the taxis are moving, the office towers are filling again. A holy day might sound like a day off, a whole day set apart from work and money. The very next verse of Surah Al-Jumu'ah doesn't tell people to stay. It sends them out the door.
screen: `SHOES FROM THE PILE BY THE DOOR.`

segments.voice: Verse ten. Pickthall: "And when the prayer is ended, then disperse in the land and seek of Allah's bounty, and remember Allah much, that ye may be successful." Three verbs. Fantashiru, disperse, spread out through the land. Wabtaghu, seek, from God's bounty, fadl, which commentators read here as earning a living. And udhkuru, remember God much. Commentators read the command to go out as a permission, not an obligation: the restriction of the previous verse is lifted. Still, the order is telling. In these verses, Friday isn't a day off. It's a day with one hour carved out for gathering, and then work resumes, with remembrance carried into it. Then verse eleven tells a story against the community itself. While the Prophet ﷺ was giving the sermon one Friday, a trade caravan arrived in Medina. People slipped out to it, and left him standing. Bukhari and Muslim report that only twelve men remained. The verse records it plainly, and adds: what is with God is better than amusement and trade, and God is the best of providers. So verses nine to eleven make a little circle. Leave trade for the prayer. After the prayer, go seek a living. But never leave the prayer for the trade. Remembrance at the center, work around it, and the word much: remember God much, not only in the mosque, but out in the market too.
screen: `DISPERSE, SEEK, REMEMBER.` · `NOT A DAY OFF.` · `THE CARAVAN AND THE TWELVE.` · `REMEMBER GOD MUCH, OUT IN THE MARKET.`

segments.voice: The practice: work well after praying. Sit, and breathe. If you pray, think of your next prayer, and the work that follows it. If you don't, think of this sit as your pause. Now picture the very next task waiting for you. See yourself starting it calmly, carrying a little of this quiet into it, doing it carefully, as if it counted. Choose one way you'll do it a little better than usual. The bell holds the time.
Fadl: God's bounty, what Surah Al-Jumu'ah tells believers to go out and seek once the Friday prayer ends. Today's word.
Your line: pray, then work. Today, after your pause, do your next task well, and remember once in the middle of it. Day six hundred twenty-seven.

howItsDone: After the Friday prayer, many Muslims return to work or business; Friday is a day of congregation rather than a required day of rest, though some countries include it in the weekend.

fork.setup: the Prophet is giving the Friday sermon. word comes that a trade caravan has arrived in town. what do many of the people do?
options: slip out to the caravan, leaving him standing.
fork.reveal: many left; only twelve remained. verse eleven records it and says what is with God is better than amusement and trade.

original.note: Arabic: then disperse in the land. Spoken right after the Friday prayer ends.

trapdoor: what you thought: Friday is the Muslim day of rest.
what it means: one hour for gathering, then back to work, with remembrance carried along.
what a scholar hears: the imperative after a prohibition read as permission (ibaha) by most usul scholars; the caravan of 62:11 in Bukhari 936 and Muslim 863; fadl read as livelihood.

sources.quoted: And when the prayer is ended, then disperse in the land and seek of Allah's bounty, and remember Allah much, that ye may be successful.

Editor review 2026-10-01: fadl no longer glossed as 'the ordinary word for earnings' (it means bounty; commentators read it as livelihood here); cut 'most jurists', the 'many Muslim-majority countries' claim, and the unsourced drums detail (voice and fork); 'not a sabbath of rest' rephrased as 'not a day off' so Friday isn't set against the Jewish Sabbath; the hook no longer tells listeners what surprises them.
